bluf: LYFE Marketing is an Atlanta social media management and advertising company for small businesses that has added PPC, email and SMS, short video, web design and, as its AI move, ChatGPT advertising management sold as a new paid channel. It publishes prices ($650 to $1,150 a month for paid search, a $500 starter website plus $97 a month) and claims $304M+ client revenue generated and 5,135+ small businesses served. The record lists no dated move. What a rival should know: it sells AI visibility while its robots.txt blocks ClaudeBot, Google-Extended and Applebot-Extended, it sells social with no Instagram, TikTok or YouTube channel linked from its own site, and displacement reads 68 on the Monsoon read, a book that buys on price.
doing:
The positioning line reads: award winning social media management and advertising company for small businesses, adding PPC, email and SMS, short video and web design. In plain words, a productised SMB social shop with channel add ons and a price list. The headline claim is $304M+ client revenue generated, $50M+ ad spend managed and 5,135+ small businesses served, aggregate claims with one described client in the record.

Service lines run from social media marketing and management and social media advertising through PPC management, email and SMS marketing, website design, short video management and short video advertising to ChatGPT advertising, branding, local SEO, white label SEO and content marketing; no proprietary product and no partner is listed. It leads with Creator & Influencer and Paid Social, both scored 3: the title and H1 brand it a social media management company with a short video management line, and the meta description lists social media advertising with Facebook, Instagram, LinkedIn and short video ad pages. Core lines scored 2 are AI Search (two dedicated pages selling ChatGPT ad campaigns built in OpenAI's Ads Manager), Email & CRM (several vertical email marketing pages), Paid Search (published tiers from $650 per month) and Web & Product (a starter plan at $500 plus $97 monthly, a claim of 400+ pages designed). B2B, content, local and SEO score 1; AI automation, CRO, Data & Measurement, programmatic and retail media score 0.

Its AI posture is ChatGPT advertising management for small businesses as a paid channel, with no GEO or AEO offer found and a robots.txt that blocks most AI crawlers: AI as a media buy, not a visibility practice. The moves list is empty, no dated launch, award or hire. Pricing is the one thing it publishes freely, paid search management at $650, $850 and $1,150 per month by ad spend band, the starter website at $500 plus $97 per month, and per service pricing pages; the Horus read still marks P5 unknown, since those are price lists rather than outputs or outcomes. Absent for an agency claiming 5,135+ clients: case study text, news, jobs, an owner, a founding year, an employee count and any measurement line.
clients:
The client type is SMB. The record lists verticals from real estate and apartments, dental, healthcare, financial services and banking, insurance, accounting and legal through franchise, construction and contractors, fitness and gyms, beauty and spas to restaurants, ecommerce and nonprofits; the home market is the US from one Atlanta office.

The needs read holds 8 clients, 1 observed and 7 named only. The observed one is Emiliana's Bake Shop, coded brand and creative because its reference sits on the branding services page. The seven slugs under the clients path name Georgia State University, Cardinal Group Companies, Chance Partners, University Towers, a barber institute, Ray Hope Christian Church and Berean Christian Church, with nothing about the work; for those the need is inferred from what LYFE Marketing leads with, social management and paid social, and the sentence says so. The slugs themselves say something the table does not: two apartment and student housing names (University Towers, Cardinal Group Companies), a university, two churches and a bakery match the vertical list of apartments, nonprofits and local trades, a book of local SMB accounts rather than brands. The shared list is empty: none of the eight appears on another tracked agency's book.

What the base needs next: the mix is best placed for KJ1, the click is being replaced by the citation, and KJ8, human provenance becomes a distribution signal, and most exposed to KJ6, the agency middle is being hollowed out, and KJ4, the platforms are absorbing the execution layer, on paid social and paid search hours. It is likely, moderate confidence, that small local accounts of this kind next need Local Services Ads and Sponsored Places work, which P3 absent says it does not sell, and roughly even chance they need the human provenance signal on social that its own site does not model, having no short form channel linked.
house:
Say and do: five lines tested, three practised, integrity 60. AI Search / GEO is contradicted: it sells AI visibility, publishes no llms.txt and blocks ClaudeBot, Google-Extended and Applebot-Extended in robots.txt, with 2 AI topic URLs in the sitemap. Creator & Influencer is contradicted: no Instagram, TikTok or YouTube channel is linked from its site, only LinkedIn, X and Facebook. Paid Search is corroborated: 70 Google ads of its own, 4 in the last 30 days, 64 of them video, last shown 2026-09-27. Paid Social is corroborated by Meta, LinkedIn Insight, TikTok, X, Reddit and Snap pixels on its own site. LinkedIn advertising is corroborated: 20 company page ads, samples reading: Real clients, real results, LYFE Marketing, and a national TV feature on The Profit with Marcus Lemonis. Both gaps flagged are the AI ones.

Content velocity is nil: the sitemap lists 988 URLs with 0 updated in 90 days and 0 in 365. The stack is GTM, GA4, Google Ads, the six social pixels, Hotjar, VWO and CallRail on WordPress, with VWO the one test tool; no ABM stack. Meta and TikTok libraries: the record is silent.
market:
Horus reads 5.2, band Neutral. Best placed for KJ1, the click is being replaced by the citation (net 0.292, AI Search / GEO and Paid Search against SEO), and KJ8, human provenance becomes a distribution signal (net 0.263, Creator & Influencer and Content & Digital PR). Most exposed to KJ6, the agency middle is being hollowed out (net minus 0.263, Paid Social, Paid Search and SEO), and KJ4, the platforms are absorbing the execution layer (net minus 0.243, Paid Social and Paid Search at minus 2 each). The mix sits at 16:28 on the Solar Arc; best fit is The Commons Rebuilt at 47/100; resilience 30.7. It is partial on P1 (audited AI visibility), P4 (paid media without first party data or measurement depth), P7 and P8 (talks ads inside assistants, no holdout capability), absent on P2, P3 and P6, unknown on P5.

The Monsoon read is 59.1, Onshore wind: migration 50.6 against displacement 67.6, Web & Product (10) and Paid Search (7) carrying the most movable hours, automation overlapping 25% of them. Shore: 65% South and Southeast Asia, 25% Latin America. The evidence class is observed through the white_label term, with icp_smb inferred; no hub office and no onshore claim is listed.
openings:
The strongest opening is the double contradiction on its own house: it sells ChatGPT advertising and AI visibility while blocking ClaudeBot, Google-Extended and Applebot-Extended and publishing no llms.txt, and it sells social media management with no Instagram, TikTok or YouTube channel linked from its site. A rival that shows open crawler access and its own live short form channels is likely, moderate confidence, to win any SMB pitch where the prospect checks. Falsifier: the robots.txt blocks lifting or a TikTok or Instagram channel appearing on lyfemarketing.com.

Second, price: displacement reads 67.6 on the Monsoon read with a white label SEO line observed, so the book buys on price and an offshore delivered rival can undercut it line by line against a published price list, very likely, moderate confidence. Third, the book is opaque: 7 of 8 clients are slugs with no described work, a question to ask the apartment, church and university accounts directly. Fourth, P3 is absent: a book of local SMB accounts with no Local Services Ads or Sponsored Places work, which an LSA led local offer undercuts. Fifth, measurement: Data & Measurement scores 0 and P4 is partial, so an offer led by first party data and measurement depth beats a $650 a month tier on proof rather than price. The sitemap is idle, 0 URLs updated in 90 days, so a live content operation is a visible contrast.
watch: Indicator I2, Alphabet Q3 2026 search growth and AI Mode ad disclosures, reads late October 2026: growth below 10% flags cannibalization and sharpens KJ1, its best placed judgment, behind the ChatGPT advertising line.
Indicator I10, Reddit US daily users against search referral volatility, reads late October 2026: US DAUq growth at or below 5% alongside AI Mode growth confirms the UGC starvation risk under KJ1.

Indicator I8, holdco Q3 organic growth, headcount and pricing model disclosures, reads October 2026: output or outcome pricing at a top five holdco would deepen KJ6, the judgment this mix is most exposed to.

Indicator I6, platform AI labeling enforcement after the EU Article 50(2) deadline, reads 2 December 2026: new reach penalties for unlabeled AI personas would strengthen KJ8 for a social shop, if it has channels to show.
Follow up whether the AI crawler blocks in robots.txt lift, whether an llms.txt appears, and whether a short form channel gets linked from the site.
